verdict.evidence:
The code observation is verbatim-accurate but the asserted vulnerability is refuted on two independent grounds.

1) Exact line confirmed — frontend/src/panels/GitPanel.tsx:137-141:
  `const result = await gitSubmit()`
  `if (result.compare_url) { window.open(result.compare_url, "_blank") }`
This is the ONLY window.open in the frontend (Grep: single hit), so no shared helper exists — accurate.

2) The claimed primitive ("newly opened tab receives a live window.opener reference ... reverse tabnabbing") does NOT hold. window.open(url, "_blank") with NO features string implicitly applies `noopener` in every browser engine this app targets (Chrome/Edge >=88, Firefox >=79, Safari >=12.1). The returned handle is null and the new tab has no live opener. tsconfig.app.json target is "ES2022" and deps are React 19.2 / Vite 6.3 — a strictly evergreen-browser app with no legacy-browser support. The vulnerable opener behavior only survived in pre-2021 browsers, which are out of scope here. The central technical assertion is therefore false for the supported platform.

3) Threat model is empty. The opened URL host is the user's own configured git remote: _build_compare_url (src/haute/_git.py:284) reads `git remote get-url origin` and returns a link ONLY for github/gitlab/dev.azure.com|visualstudio.com/bitbucket, returning None for any unknown host (line 310). Reverse tabnabbing requires the OPENED page to be attacker-controlled; an attacker who controls your origin remote URL already owns your repository, so opener access to a local pricing-tool tab is no escalation. The "read the referrer" concern is also moot — these are first-party hosts you navigate to deliberately.
verdict.refined_severity: trivial/non-issue (below low) — defense-in-depth lint nit, not an exploitable bug under the supported browsers and own-remote threat model
verdict.recommended_fix: Optional hardening only: change to window.open(result.compare_url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer") for explicitness/lint-cleanliness. No behavioral security change on supported browsers; do not treat as a security finding.

verdict.evidence: Code-trace confirms the claim end to end. GitPanel.tsx:133-147 `handleSubmit`: `const result = await gitSubmit(); if (result.compare_url) { window.open(result.compare_url, "_blank") } await refresh()`. There is no `else` branch and no success toast/banner/state, even though `addToast` is imported (line 31) and used for success/error elsewhere (e.g. loadHistory, line 75). Backend `submit_for_review` (_git.py:837-869) pushes the branch when a remote exists (lines 850-858) then returns `GitSubmitResponse(compare_url=compare_url, branch=branch, pushed=pushed, ...)` with NO exception, where `compare_url = _build_compare_url(...)` (line 861). `_build_compare_url` (_git.py:284-310) returns None when there is no remote (`if not raw_url: return None`, lines 287-288) and None for any host that is not github/gitlab/azure/bitbucket (line 310). The response is parsed by `parseGitSubmitResponse` (guards.ts:1849-1857), which uses `optionalNullableString` for `compare_url` (line 1852), so `null` passes validation and the promise resolves — the frontend `catch` is never entered. Net result on a no-remote or unrecognised/self-hosted git host: branch is pushed, `refresh()` runs, but the user gets no confirmation and no link/instruction for where to open the PR.
verdict.recommended_fix: In `handleSubmit`, handle the `compare_url === null` (and no-remote) case explicitly using the data the backend already returns. When `result.compare_url` is falsy, show a success toast such as `addToast("success", result.pushed ? \`Pushed ${result.branch}. Open a pull request on your git host.\` : \`Committed to ${result.branch}. No remote configured to push to.\`)`. Optionally add a success toast on the happy path too. This uses the existing `pushed`/`branch` fields (types.ts:937-942) so no backend change is required.

verdict.evidence: GitPanel.tsx: the popover is gated only on open-state, not on data. Line 322 `{branchDropdownOpen && (<div className="absolute ... rounded-lg shadow-2xl ... border ...">` then four sibling sections each guarded by `.length > 0` (line 325 protectedBranches, 334 yourBranches, 348 otherBranches, 362 archivedBranches) with NO else/empty child. Grep confirms there is no "No branches" string and no min-height on the popover (only `min-h-0` on the unrelated outer scroll container, line 289). The toggle button (line 308) has no `disabled` guard, so it is clickable while `branches===[]`. branches initial state is [] (line 35); refresh() runs async on mount (line 67) and on error never calls setBranches (lines 62-64), so during the pre-resolution window, on a fetch error, or for a branch-less repo, opening the dropdown renders a bordered/shadowed box with zero children. CLAIM CORRECT for the empty-list case. However the candidate's Scenario B ("a repo that exposes only the current non-protected branch which is filtered out of every group") is REFUTED by trace: lines 216-219 make `otherBranches` a catch-all (`!is_yours && !is_archived && !["main","master","develop"].includes(name)`); backend _git.py list_branches (lines 528-537) emits every refs/heads ref, and each maps to exactly one of the four buckets — no branch escapes all four. So the empty popover only occurs when the list is genuinely empty (mount race, fetch error, or zero-branch repo), not for a "filtered-out" branch. In normal operation main/master always exists, so protectedBranches is non-empty and the box has content.
verdict.recommended_fix:
Add an empty-state fallback inside the popover: after the four `.length > 0` sections, render a "No branches" message (or render it conditionally when `branches.length === 0`), e.g. `{branches.length === 0 && (
No branches
)}`. Distinguish loading from empty if desired (track a loaded flag). Note the candidate's "filtered-out single branch" scenario is not a real trigger; correct the description to "empty branch list (pre-load race / fetch error / branch-less repo)".

verdict.evidence:
CONFIRMED that `branches` and `subBranches` are parsed independently and indexed by the SAME idx, with no alignment step. CalculationHero.tsx:458-459 `const branches = parseBranches(expression.expression_text)` / `const subBranches = parseBranches(calculation.substituted_text)`; :470-473 `isBranchMatched(idx){ const sub = subBranches[idx]; ... return sub.result.includes(resultStr) }`; :481-486 maps over `branches` and, when `backendTakenBranchIndex === null`, calls `isBranchMatched(idx)` with the branches-index. No code re-aligns subBranches to branches by condition/position. So if the two arrays differ in length/order, `subBranches[idx]` is the wrong branch.

However the candidate OVERSTATES the divergence risk. Scenario (b) ("backend substituted_text can have a different branch shape") is REFUTED by the backend: _expression_parser.py:1375 `substituted_text = _substitute_values(parsed.expression_text, input_values)` derives substituted_text from the SAME `expression_text` string by replacing only column-name tokens via word-boundary regex (_replace_column_name, :1500-1508). The `when`/`then`/`otherwise` keyword skeleton (built at _format_when_clauses :664,:667 as "when {c} then {t}" / "otherwise {o}") is preserved verbatim, so the normal-case parses are positionally aligned by construction. Every fallback test in CalculationHero.test.tsx (l.732,756,817,838) models substituted_text as a structurally-identical substitution — and the existing test at l.784 shows the team already routes the ambiguous "multiple branches same value" case through the backend `taken_branch_index` instead of isBranchMatched.

The path is reachable but narrow. backendTakenBranchIndex===null (CalculationHero.tsx:460-463) only for a real conditional when _evaluate_conditional_branches returns taken_branch_index=None — i.e. _expression_parser.py:1457/1473 returns `{}` (SyntaxError or best_match None) or _eval_clauses (:2082-2114) falls through with no truthy cond AND no otherwise (returns None, result is null). The ONLY scenario (a) that can actually mis-split one array but not the other is a column whose substituted VALUE embeds a bare ` when `/` then `/` otherwise ` token (e.g. a string value "reopened when escalated", quoted by _format_value :1523-1524), shifting the frontend regex /when\s+(.+?)\s+then.../gi split for substituted_text only. A literal containing those words in the expression itself splits identically in both, so stays aligned. Net: a genuine latent off-by-branch in the legacy fallback, requiring (parse-failure-or-no-match) AND an adversarial keyword-bearing string value, affecting only branch HIGHLIGHTING in the trace UI — never a pricing result.
verdict.recommended_fix: In the fallback path, stop indexing subBranches by the expression-text branch index. Either (a) gate the whole substituted-text heuristic away now that the backend reliably emits taken_branch_index for any taken branch (and treat backendTakenBranchIndex===null as "no branch highlighted"), or (b) align by matching subBranches to branches positionally only when `branches.length === subBranches.length`, otherwise skip highlighting. Add a frontend test where a referenced column's value contains the literal word "when"/"otherwise" (e.g. expression `when status == 'x' then a otherwise b`, input_values status="re when y") with taken_branch_index omitted, asserting no wrong branch is marked data-matched=true.
